fact.claim: Each Site-to-Site VPN connection has two tunnels, and a standard VPN tunnel supports up to 1.25 Gbps (the VPN FAQ states this value for each tunnel; the quotas page gives it for a standard tunnel). For a connection to a virtual private gateway, aggregated throughput limits apply.
fact.question: What is the approximate maximum throughput of a Site-to-Site VPN connection tunnel, according to the VPN FAQ?

values.spoken: one point two five gigabits per second

qualifiers.scope: per standard VPN tunnel; a connection has two tunnels
qualifiers.condition: connection to a virtual private gateway: aggregated throughput limits apply

evidence.quote: Each AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection has two tunnels and each tunnel supports a maximum throughput of up to 1.25 Gbps. If your VPN connection is to a Virtual Private Gateway, aggregated throughput limits would apply.
evidence.title: AWS VPN | FAQs | Amazon Web Services (AWS)

evidence.quote: | Maximum bandwidth per standard VPN tunnel | Up to 1.25 Gbps | No |
evidence.title: AWS Site-to-Site VPN quotas

fact.note: FAQ question: 'What is the approximate maximum throughput of a Site-to-Site VPN connection?' (item 16). Large bandwidth tunnels (5 Gbps) are covered by facts from the user guide.
fact.author: mine-12-faq

votes.reason: The quote states two tunnels per connection, each up to 1.25 Gbps, with aggregated limits on a virtual private gateway.

Since 2025-11-12 a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel can support up to 5 Gbps (large bandwidth tunnel; modifiable between standard and large since 2026-05-06); 'each tunnel up to 1.25 Gbps' is true only for standard tunnels.
votes.quote: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports VPN connections with up to 5 Gbps bandwidth per tunnel, a 4x improvement from existing limit of 1.25 Gbps.
